notes: Access: direct HTTP (Magento 2 GraphQL) plus Playwright render (SPA storefront). Main nav (both the raw GraphQL categoryList tree and the rendered header/footer captured via Playwright) leads with a top-level item literally named 'NEW IN' (category id 362, url /en-uae/season-latest.html, no children). This is a strong target-term match ('New In' is one of the brief's listed target terms). Applied the Collection-page test: opened the rendered page - it has a real breadcrumb 'HOME > NEW IN', an on-page heading 'NEW IN' with copy 'Recently arrived. Already timeless. Discover new silhouettes, materials, and statement pieces shaped by global craft and modern restraint, thoughtfully introduced to evolve your space.', and a genuine sortable/filterable product grid (Relevance/Color/Material sort+filter controls, 20 products rendered per page via Klevu infinite scroll) - not an editorial/campaign landing page. The page's own <meta title> is explicitly 'Buy New Arrivals and Home Decor Collection Online | Marina Home Interiors', confirming the site's own framing of this page as New Arrivals. qty verified two independent ways: (1) Klevu categoryPath merchandising API (eucs26v2.ksearchnet.com/cs/v2/search, searchedTerm='*', the same live product-count source used by the prior Home-Decor pass for this company) returned meta.totalResultsFound=63; (2) Magento GraphQL products(filter:{category_id:{eq:362}}).total_count also =63. Both agree exactly (the raw Magento categoryList.product_count field shows an inflated 67, which is NOT used, per the known trap documented in the prior Home-Decor pass notes for this company). Checked sitemap (~3760 URLs) and nav for any additional New Arrivals-shaped URLs (new-arrivals, new-in, just-in, whats-new, latest) via GraphQL urlResolver - none resolved except season-latest.html itself, so this is the sole New Arrivals listing, no genuine sub-structure to preserve. No Arabic-language equivalent surfaced as a separate listing (same category id, shared catalogue).
